insights.insight: $4.51M in cryptographically verified GMV across 83,856+ receipts represents a deterministic purchase signal at scale — not a modeled proxy, but confirmed transactions with category, brand, and basket-size attribution.

The network is adding approximately 454 receipts per day with no compression in that rate over a 102-day observation window, giving brands a stable and growing pool of verified buyers to target against.

Grocery-supermarkets (1,406 receipts, ~$40.47 average basket) and restaurants-dining (1,212 receipts, ~$31.55) together account for 52% of 14-day verified volume — category-level purchase frequency sufficient to build audience cohorts without probabilistic inference.

Walmart holds 368 of 5,013 visible 14-day receipts (7.3% of verified volume) with Costco, Kroger, and Publix each above 150 receipts — brand-specific purchase confirmation at a granularity that probabilistic targeting cannot replicate.

The 7-day average basket (~$42.34) running above the 14-day average (~$39.70) indicates recent transaction sizes are holding or modestly firming, giving media buyers a near-real-time read on buyer quality within the network.

The core pricing asymmetry holds: the industry pays $5+ CPM for probabilistic purchase inference while verified receipt data — confirming a specific transaction at a specific retailer — remains structurally underpriced relative to its targeting precision.
